items.q: The book's caution while interpreting flash pulmonary edema in this context is:
opts: Every pulmonary edema is cardiac unless proven otherwise
Every pulmonary edema is renal unless proven otherwise
Flash pulmonary edema excludes cardiac disease
Pulmonary edema never occurs in bilateral RAS
items.exp: Note: every pulmonary edema is cardiac unless proven otherwise. (Book p752)

items.q: The screening test named on this page is renal artery stenosis colour doppler ultrasound (CDU); its characteristic waveform clue is the:
items.exp: Screening test: RAS colour doppler ultrasound (CDU); look for parvus tardus pattern. (Book p752)

items.q: On CDU, a resistivity index (RI) at or above which value points to parenchymal disease (CKD)?
With RI < 0.8, the stenosis criteria that route the patient to CT/MR renal angiography are:
opts: Peak systolic velocity > 180 cm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.05
Peak systolic velocity > 100 cm/s OR RAR > 2.5 OR ΔRI > 0.01
Peak systolic velocity > 250 cm/s OR RAR > 5 OR ΔRI > 0.1
Peak systolic velocity > 180 mm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.5
items.exp: RI < 0.8 with PSV > 180 cm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.05 → CT/MR renal angiography (IOC). (Book p752)

items.q: All of the following are CDU look-for criteria of RAS EXCEPT:
items.exp: The book's velocity criterion is peak systolic velocity > 180 cm/s, not 80 cm/s. (Book p752)

items.q: The IOC after a positive screen is CT/MR renal angiography; the gold standard that is both diagnostic and therapeutic is:
items.exp: Conventional angiograph (gold standard): diagnostic and therapeutic. (Book p752)

items.q: Which statement about fibromuscular dysplasia is TRUE?
opts: It is a non-atherosclerotic, non-inflammatory arteriopathy most common in young girls
It is an atherosclerotic disease of elderly males
It is an inflammatory vasculitis of the proximal aorta
items.exp: Non atherosclerotic/non inflammatory arteriopathy; incident: m/c in young girls. (Book p752)

items.q: The pathology of fibromuscular dysplasia is medial fibroplasia in the tunica media of the:
items.exp: Involves middle to distal renal artery: medial fibroplasia in tunica media. (Book p752)

items.q: Fibromuscular dysplasia is bilateral in the renal arteries in 25% of cases; the other 25% involve:
items.exp: 25% B/L renal artery, 25% involves cerebral vessels. (Book p752)

items.q: The angiographic feature illustrated for medial fibromuscular dysplasia is the:
items.exp: The "string of beads" feature in medial fibromuscular dysplasia. (Book p752)
